reading.body:
Equinix DC11 in Ashburn is a 116,831 square-foot facility with N+1 redundancy in both power and cooling, but the operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this building. Without disclosed power consumption, its actual compute density relative to other Virginia facilities cannot be determined from public information.

DC11 belongs to Equinix's 15-facility Washington DC metro region, which spans Ashburn, Manassas, and Culpeper and functions as North America's largest peering point. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 publish power capacity; DC11 is not among them. Among the 23 Virginia facilities with published figures totaling 1,375 MW, this campus ranks 24th, meaning it either falls below the smallest disclosed capacity or remains unpublished alongside the 303 other unmeasured sites in the state.

The building's redundancy specifications qualify it for mission-critical colocation workloads requiring continuous operation. Whether DC11 matters to AI scaling depends on undisclosed power availability. Equinix has not published the megawatt figure needed to assess whether this facility contributes materially to the region's AI infrastructure capacity or merely maintains legacy colocation demand.
